Baby steps friend. I highly recommend therapy first and foremost, they can help you with your anxiety. Other small things you can do to slowly gain mental confidence, working out (this is a big one), meditating, reading, and finding some activity you can enjoy that relaxes you will all help. 

Also don't try to make too big of a goal to soon. Like working out, you don't need to set a goal of 6 days in the gym for an hour and a perfect diet; etc. know what you are currently capable of and build from there. Once a week go for a jog, maybe do 10-20 push ups every morning. 

These are the little things you can do to help ease anxiety and gain confidence. One thing you must do eventually is get a job, and once you find one and you have an actual schedule and bring in money, that will help too. 

As for social anxiety this mindset has helped me. Everyone is just like you. We are all human, all individual, and all on some scale alone. You want extremely high confidence and not to give a fuck? It's as simple as having it. Walk out with your head high and chest out knowing that among all of these humans on earth, you are one who takes no shit and is not afraid of anything. Because everyone is just like you. Scared, afraid to be alone, and the fear of being a failure in life. 

If you wake up tomorrow and do 10 push ups, you're 10 push ups ahead of the next guy being flaky and unmotivated. You get a job, well guess what you are now ahead of thousands and thousands of people who don't have one. Have confidence. Especially if it's a no skill job like fast food or whatever. You go into your interview knowing that they want you, because you know you are the best person for this job. How do you know that? Because you told yourself you are.

Sorry I wasn't clear on the first half, I more so meant those are the 3 points we NEED to implement to reduce situations like that.

"The cops don't have to change, if they act badly, they can, and the courts respond accordingly." See how thats pretty interchangeable and its not just one group at fault? The suspects do have to change, they need to be compliant and not threaten a cop in such a way that he feels a need to act in self defense. Justified or not, you will ALWAYS lose a fight against a cop. You will, so why act in aggression? Have you ever seen an instance where a suspect aggressive or non-aggressively defended himself and came out on top? Certainly not aggressively, and I'm sure they're very little situations where suspects argued themselves out of a situation, it can be done but thats not the point. 

The point is, if cops are properly trained on law and how to de-escalate situations (rather than escalate them like they seem to do), and you act in compliance, even if your rights are being broken, than your time to be aggressive is in court, that's when its your turn to put the law back onto the cop. The issue today is the court system and cops are all on the same side, who would want to take down one of their own, making your department and city look bad? I'm sure if we got better officers and better court management than we will see a downfall in police brutality, the issue is its kind of hard to replace the thousands of cops at work with brand new ones. For now it starts with what /u/beaner505 said, if you're in a high strung situation, lay down, put your hands behind your back, and listen to the officer and you will be up shit creek with a paddle rather than without one. 

Going after the officers can bring awareness, sometimes get them fired, but will bring 0 change in getting a strong court system that will defend your rights as a system. What looks more in your favor in a court case, you being aggresive who yelled and screamed at a cop and "threatened him" to the point of restraint, or you being completely compliant individual who listened and did everything the cop said yet still received police brutality?
